- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% from peak to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted mean by 3–7% to account for lagged correction.  
- If forecasted price exceeds 75% of the 30-day historical high, apply a downward bias of 5–10% to prevent overconfidence in upward trends.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by reducing volatility in 3–5 day windows to avoid erratic swings.
